subject: Computer Networking
title: Internet Exchange Points
description: A fast breakdown of Internet Exchange Points for builders.

hook.text: Thousands of internet providers exist. They don't each run cables to every other. They meet at exchange points.

buildup.text: An IXP is a physical building where networks plug in and swap traffic. Like a postal sorting facility.

discovery.text: Major IXPs in Frankfurt, London, and Virginia handle terabits of traffic per second, 24/7.

twist.text: Without IXPs, your data to a neighbor's ISP might route through a distant city. IXPs keep traffic local.

climax.text: Countries with strong IXPs have faster, cheaper internet. Those without depend on expensive transit links.

punchline.text: IXPs are where the internet's roads actually meet.

quiz.question: What is an Internet Exchange Point?
options: A physical location where different networks connect to exchange traffic
A software tool for monitoring bandwidth
A government agency that regulates internet use

details.summary: Internet Exchange Points are physical locations where different networks connect and exchange traffic directly. IXPs reduce latency by letting nearby networks communicate without routing through distant intermediaries. Major IXPs handle terabits of traffic and are critical infrastructure.
details.whyItMatters: IXPs keep local traffic local. Without them, a message between two networks in the same city might travel across a continent through a Tier 1 carrier.
takeaways: IXPs let networks exchange traffic directly in one physical location
They reduce latency by keeping local traffic on local paths
Major IXPs handle terabits of traffic per second

faq.question: Why do networks peer at IXPs instead of using transit?
faq.answer: Peering is free or much cheaper than buying transit from a Tier 1 carrier. It also reduces latency because traffic flows directly between networks. High-traffic networks save millions in transit costs by peering. IXPs make peering efficient by providing a shared location.

faq.question: Where are the largest IXPs located?
faq.answer: DE-CIX in Frankfurt, AMS-IX in Amsterdam, and LINX in London are among the world's largest. They handle multiple terabits per second. Major IXPs exist in every region. Their locations reflect historical internet development and business concentration.
